# Aviary golden vectors - subchains version 2 (dynamic registration,
# Merkle registry, closing, persistence). docs/design/SUBCHAINS.md Part 2.
#
# Generated by tools/print_subchain_vectors.cpp, which runs the scenario in
# tests/subchain_vectors.hpp through the C ABI. The C++ suite
# (test_subchain_vectors), the Go binding and the Dart binding replay the
# same calls and must reproduce every line exactly.
#
# Scenario. Keys: registrar and record author = the Ed25519 key from the
# seed 32 x 0xA0 (registrar_secret below, seed || public); main chain
# validator = BLS key from 32 x 0x01; user chain validator = BLS key from
# 32 x 0x10. Every genesis is aviary_genesis_build(chain_id, timestamp 1,
# assurance 1, state model 2, no accounts, one validator of power 1) with
# the blueprint bft / record.
#   main chain 1: dynamic policy (max_depth 1, no other bound, threshold 1,
#     one Ed25519 registrar, no genesis children).
#   user chain 1001: bound to the main chain's genesis hash.
#   main block 1 (timestamp 10): registers chain 1001 (epoch 0, no expiry).
#   user blocks 1 and 2 (timestamps 20, 21): block 1 writes key 32 x 0x42 =
#     "door opened" (nonce 0, op 0).
#   main block 2 (timestamp 11): anchors both user headers.
#   main block 3 (timestamp 12): closes chain 1001 at its recorded tip.
#   wide chain 2: same policy; block 1 (timestamp 10) registers chains 2000
#     to 2010, each with the user validator; the proof is for chain 2007.
# *_hash of a snapshot is BLAKE3-256 of the aviary_chain_snapshot bytes,
# taken with the block archive enabled from genesis on both chains.
#
# Format: <name> <hex>
